note: SPEC.md Section 13 — template logic is data, not code, so DRAFTT and any other framework can be added without touching the engine. Targets are decimal fractions of the template's `basis` income, keyed by the bucket ids in expense_categories.json. The classic 50/30/20 is defined against take-home pay, so `basis` is "net" and the engine derives it from gross using the effective-tax lookup rather than asking for a second income figure. A template with `targets: null` is a method rather than a split and is compared differently.

templates.blurb: Half to needs, a third to wants, a fifth to savings and extra debt.
A higher-cost-of-living variant that concedes more to needs.

templates.label: Zero-based
templates.blurb: Every dollar gets a job. There is no target split — the test is whether income minus everything assigned lands on zero.
